newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lorry drivers action hits airlines at Bordeaux.
newsitem.headline: Lorry drivers action hits airlines at Bordeaux.

text.p: Several airlines based at Bordeaux airport say trucking services for airfreight are being badly affected by industrial action by French lorry drivers.
Over the past two days, thousands of lorries have blocked major routes in various regions of France.
The drivers demands cover wage increases, working hours and retirement at 55.
Union representatives were meeting this afternoon to decide on whether to continue their action.
"Since Monday (November 18) we have had a truck blocked in traffic at numerous points in France and we still don't know when it is going to arrive," a Bordeaux-based Lufthansa official told Reuters.
The truck had come from Frankfurt and was en route for Bilbao via Bordeaux, the official said.
"For export traffic, we are managing to get shipments up to Paris/CDG by using combined transport road and rail and from there to our main hub Frankfurt."
However, Lufthansa's trucking services between Frankfurt and Bordeaux had been suspended until further notice, the official added.

Meanwhile, an Air France Cargo official at Bordeaux said one of its trucks had been blocked in traffic "somewhere between Paris and Bordeaux" since while another had had to turn back to the French carrier's hub at CDG.

Air France had offloaded some freight from trucks, in particular perishables and transferred it on to Air France Europe's passenger services between Bordeaux and Paris but for bigger size shipments this was not a solution, the official said.
"Tonight (Wednesday) we'll chance our luck and try to get a truck on its way to Paris but quite frankly we don't know how far it will get !"
Dutch carrier, KLM, said one of its trucks was blocked between Toulouse and Bordeaux at Cahors and overall its trucking operation in south-west France was seriously disrupted.

"Having no on-line air services from Bordeaux we are getting other airlines to transport some of our freight to Paris on our behalf but bigger shipments are effectively blocked here for the moment." -ends-
Union representatives were meeting this afternoon to decide on whether to continue their action. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
